newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 92 -1 on last week
Cow (85 CL) 76 n/c
Shank (90 CL) 82 +2

Chucks (85 CL) 78 +1
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 149 +3 on last week

AMLC COMMENTARY: A much larger yarding brought a sudden halt to the upward price trend evident in cattle markets since mid June this week. Across Queensland, saleyards brimmed with over 23,000 cattle, nearly half again on last week, and the highest since June 1995 and, before that, April 1994.

In New South Wales (NSW) and Victoria, the rise in numbers was less extraordinary but definitely of the same ilk - overall yardings rose 29 percent at Dubbo in NSW and 14 percent across Livestock Market Reporting Service centres in Victoria.
By far the best news for cattle markets this week came late today in the form of another Korean tender.
The tender calls for 9458 tonnes shipped weight and includes 4200 tonnes of grassfed quarter beef, 828 tonnes of grassfed fullsets and 600 tonnes of grainfed quarters.
Bidding for this tender is next Friday November 8 and results will be available on Monday November 11.

Prices in the U.S. lean grinding beef complex were lower for both US domestic and imported product this week, as the U.S. autumn cow run continues to provide a high cow slaughter rate, bolstering production of US domestically produced lean beef.
For week ending 24 October, total U.S. cattle slaughter stood at 667,000 head, one percent more than in the previous week, but two percent lower than a year earlier.
The market for Australian lean grinding meat was mixed this week and prices were mostly lower.

Several market participants reported increased activity based on lower prices, whilst others reported a weak market due to the pressure on the U.S. domestic cattle market and the sale of beef to other countries.
The cooler weather in Japan has seen consumer demand for beef starting to recover this week.
Some retailers report that beef sales are back to normal for this time of year, especially for thinly sliced beef.
Others report that steak items and blades, for roasts etc, are still a little weak, although definitely a lot stronger than several months ago.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
